raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

This PR supersedes #52226 by porting the NVIDIA Confidential Computing (CC) decode optimizations to the V2 GPU model runner, and fixes the UVA incoherence bug that makes V2 produce garbage under CC. 

The incoherence issue with UVA was initially reported in #57224 and independently fixed by @juhiechandra in #57404 via a runtime coherence probe in `is_uva_available()`. This PR instead gates UVA on CC detection and adds a staged-copy fallback so that disabling UVA does not reintroduce host-synchronous copy stalls.

### Background

NVIDIA Confidential Computing protects workloads in confidential VMs by encrypting PCIe traffic through bounce buffers. This has two consequences for the V2 runner:

1. **Pinned host memory is not coherent from the device.** The V2 runner's `UvaBufferPool` writes inputs into pinned host memory and has the GPU read them directly through the UVA mapping. Under CC the GPU sees a stale snapshot of that memory, so the model runner produces garbage.
2. **`cudaMemcpyAsync` on pinned memory is host-synchronous.** The issuing thread blocks until the copy, and everything already queued on its stream, completes. This causes:
   - **H2D input copies** on the compute stream to block the scheduler thread behind the in-flight forward pass.
   - **Per-step D2H token readback** to delay the next CUDA graph launch.

### Changes

All changes are gated on CC detection; non-CC code paths are untouched.

- **CC detection**: `Platform.is_confidential_compute()`, auto-detected via NVML on CUDA with a `VLLM_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE=0/1` override.
- **UVA disabled under CC**: `is_uva_available()` returns `False` under CC, so the buffer pool falls back to explicit copies. A new `StagedH2DBuffer` mirrors each pinned host buffer into a device tensor on every `uva()` call, keeping the pool's invariant that a slot is only reused once no GPU reader is in flight.
- **Staged H2D input copies**: `staged_h2d()` in `vllm/v1/conf_compute_utils.py` issues the host-synchronous copy on an idle prep stream so the host only waits for the transfer itself, then orders the compute stream after it with `wait_stream` / `record_stream`. `async_tensor_h2d()` routes through this path under CC, so call sites in `encoder_decoder.py`, `encoder_only.py`, and `zero_block_ids()` need no CC-specific logic.
- **Deferred D2H output readback**: `AsyncOutput` and `AsyncPoolingOutput` record a source-ready event on the main stream at construction and issue the D2H copies from `get_output()` on the executor's output thread, instead of blocking the scheduler thread.

## Test Plan

- New unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_conf_compute_copies.py` covering UVA availability under CC, `staged_h2d()` with pinned and pageable sources, `async_tensor_h2d()` routing, `StagedH2DBuffer` pool round-trips, and deferred D2H semantics.
- Decode benchmark on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, B300, CC enabled, comparing against the V2 runner with CC off and against the V2 runner on `main` with CC on.

## Test Result

Decode throughput (output tok/s per GPU). Slowdown is the increase in time per output token relative to CC off.

| Concurrency | CC off | main, CC on | This PR, CC on | Slowdown before | Slowdown after |
|------------:|-------:|------------:|---------------:|----------------:|---------------:|
| 4           | 129    | 85          | 118            | 51.8%           | 9.3%           |
| 8           | 212    | 147         | 198            | 44.2%           | 7.1%           |
| 16          | 352    | 250         | 322            | 40.8%           | 9.3%           |
| 32          | 534    | 397         | 490            | 34.5%           | 9.0%           |
| 64          | 796    | 617         | 741            | 29.0%           | 7.4%           |
| 128         | 1229   | 953         | 1120           | 29.0%           | 9.7%           |

The per-token CC slowdown drops from 29–52% to 7–10% across all concurrencies, bringing CC throughput to 91–93% of the non-CC baseline.

🚀

CC-hardware validation data for this PR's premise (this is not a review of the diff, and I have not yet tested this PR's head). The runs were AI-assisted (Claude Code); I ran them and reviewed the output.

**Setup:** Azure `Standard_NCC40ads_H100_v5` (H100 NVL), CC ON per `nvidia-smi conf-compute -f`, driver 595.71.05, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Qwen3-8B, random 1024/256 tokens.

1. **Host-synchronous copies confirmed on H100 NVL.** A standalone microbench (#60338, [results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60338#issuecomment-6041789699)) shows pinned H2D/D2H on a busy stream blocking the host for ~19.9 ms, vs ~51 us on an idle stream. A decode loop with staged H2D + D2H worker is x1.46 (3 ms forward) / x1.14 (10 ms) vs sync, while async scheduling alone is x1.00. Reproduced on two separate VMs.
2. **V1 with #52226's copy optimizations is correct and faster with async on.** Output tok/s at concurrency 4 / 32: async on 569 / 2864 vs 468-478 / 2519-2555 for async off or optimizations off (+12-19%).
3. **V2 under CC without a UVA guard returns wrong output.** On a branch with #52226 but not this PR, forced V2 and the V2 default both produced junk (URL fragments, runs of `!` and `1`) on 8/8 greedy prompts, while V1 was correct. That reproduces #57224 on H100 NVL, which this PR's UVA gating addresses.

**Offer:** I can run the same sweep plus the output check against `c8309e4215` on this hardware and post the results here.

**Question:** would you want PPCIe/NVLE-aware detection (`nvmlSystemGetConfComputeSettings`, `multiGpuMode`) as a small follow-up PR? My understanding is that Hopper PPCIe reports `ccFeature` OFF but still uses bounce buffers; I have not been able to test that mode.

Thank you @Alex-Carter01 for the detailed measurements!

The v1 patch PR is indeed not intended to resolve the garbage output under V2, **but this PR should** (along with performance improvements). 

It would be very helpful to get a third party validation of this PR, so a run against the current head on your H100 NVL would be much appreciated. Greedy coherence on all prompts plus tok/s at a couple of concurrencies is plenty.

@ybgao-nvidia Third-party validation of this PR on a different CC platform from @Alex-Carter01's. The setup is an Azure NCC H100 NVL with an **AMD SEV-SNP** guest and the GPU in CC mode, on the same machine type where #57224, #57562 and #57680 were reported.

**Setup.** `vllm==0.31.0` wheel, torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.0.post1 with the matching jit-cache, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (MoE), async scheduling on. The `vllm/` files of this PR's head (`5bb8a5cf`) were applied to the wheel; they applied cleanly. Three configs ran back to back on one VM, with a server restart between them.

| config | greedy output vs V1 | c=1 tok/s | c=12 tok/s | #57562 repro |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | reference | 145.8 (145.0–145.9) | 1275.3 (1253.5–1278.1) | 12/12, engine alive |
| V2, unpatched 0.31.0 | 0/8, unrelated tokens | 40.6 (40.6–61.7), bimodal | 318.7 (291.4–377.2) | EngineCore dies in round 1 (`num_output_placeholders >= 0`) |
| **V2 + this PR** | **8/8 byte-identical** | **243.0 (242.9–243.1)** | **1984.6 (1981.4–1986.2)** | 12/12, engine alive |

c=1 is per-stream decode tok/s and c=12 is aggregate output tok/s. Each request is 512 tokens with `ignore_eos`, median of 5 runs (range in brackets). The repro is the chunked-prefill concurrency script from #57562, run as 6 concurrent requests × 2 rounds.

The startup log shows the intended path: `NVIDIA Confidential Computing detected via NVML`, then `Using staged H2D input copies under Confidential Computing`, and `Using V2 Model Runner`.

With this PR, V2 under CC is correct and runs 67% faster than V1 at c=1 and 56% faster at c=12 on this model. Unpatched 0.31.0 still shows all three original symptoms.

I can re-run it on a later head if that would help.

Thank you @yeighta for the insights and measurements! I'm glad to see correctness and performance improvements also on H100. 

It would be also nice to measure on head-of-PR, but we should expect to see similar performance as what we previously observe.

@ybgao-nvidia as requested, here is a run on the current head (`5bb8a5cf43`) on H100 NVL, complementary to @yeighta's SEV-SNP / MoE result above. AI-assisted (Claude Code); I ran it and reviewed the results.

**Setup:** Azure `Standard_NCC40ads_H100_v5` (H100 NVL), CC ON, driver 595.71.05, torch 2.13.0+cu130, dense `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, random 1024/256 tokens, one run per arm. Precompiled wheel from the PR's base (`ce49174247`) with the PR's Python on top. `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` for every arm (the image has no nvcc).

| Arm | Config | Greedy match (8 prompts) | Output tok/s, c=4 | c=32 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stock | defaults (V2, async on) | reference, text is correct | 577 | 2327 |
| F1 | `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 --no-async-scheduling` | 8/8 | 444 | 2038 |
| control | `VLLM_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE=0` (CC path off while CC is on) | **0/8**, junk output | n/a | n/a |

So under CC, V2 with this PR returns correct text, and switching the CC path off on the same CC-on GPU reproduces the garbage output. Async on is +30% / +14% over async off at c=4 / 32.

An earlier run on the previous head (`c8309e4215`, a different VM) gave the same correctness result and 575 / 2759 (stock) and 442 / 2344 (async off), so c=4 is identical and c=32 is 13-16% lower on this VM for both arms. Both arms moved together, which looks like VM-to-VM variance rather than the one-commit change, but I can't separate the two from one run each.

**Limits:** one GPU model, one run per arm, so differences of a few percent are within noise; PPCIe/NVLE not tested. I'm happy to repeat the run or try another model if useful.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Copy helpers for NVIDIA Confidential Computing.
+
+Under bounce-buffer Confidential Computing a host<->device
+``cudaMemcpyAsync`` is host-synchronous: the issuing thread blocks until the
+copy, and everything already queued on its stream, completes. An H2D issued
+on the compute stream therefore blocks the engine for the in-flight forward,
+and the per-step D2H readback blocks the thread that issues it.
+
+``staged_h2d`` issues uploads on an idle prep stream instead, so the host only
+pays the transfer itself. ``vllm.utils.torch_utils.async_tensor_h2d`` and the
+V2 model runner's buffer pools dispatch to it under Confidential Computing;
+outside Confidential Computing nothing here is used.
+"""
+
+from functools import cache
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+@cache
+def confidential_compute_enabled() -> bool:
+    """Whether NVIDIA Confidential Computing is active on this platform."""
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+    return current_platform.is_confidential_compute()
+
+
+@cache
+def _prep_stream_for_index(device_index: int) -> torch.cuda.Stream:
+    logger.info_once(
+        "Using staged H2D input copies under Confidential Computing "
+        "(H2D on a dedicated prep stream + D2D on the compute stream) to "
+        "avoid blocking the scheduler on the in-flight forward."
+    )
+    return torch.cuda.Stream(device=torch.device(f"cuda:{device_index}"))
+
+
+def prep_stream(device: torch.device) -> torch.cuda.Stream:
+    """Return the per-device prep stream.
+
+    A single stream suffices: every pinned H2D on it is host-synchronous under
+    Confidential Computing, so the stream is drained by the time each copy
+    call returns.
+    """
+    idx = (
+        device.index
+        if device.index is not None
+        else torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+    )
+    return _prep_stream_for_index(idx)
+
+
+def staged_h2d(
+    src: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    device: torch.device | str | None = None,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Upload a host tensor without blocking on the compute stream.
+
+    The H2D is issued on the idle prep stream, so the host only waits for the
+    transfer itself. Without ``out`` the fresh device tensor is returned with
+    its lifetime tied to the compute stream: it was allocated on the prep
+    stream, and ``record_stream`` keeps the caching allocator from recycling it
+    before the consuming kernel has run. With ``out`` the upload lands in a
+    staging tensor and an asynchronous D2D on the compute stream moves it into
+    ``out``, so an in-flight reader of ``out`` is never overwritten.
+
+    ``src`` must already have the destination dtype: a converting copy would
+    run its cast kernel on the prep stream, unordered with the compute stream.
+    A pageable ``src`` is not host-synchronous under Confidential Computing, so
+    the compute stream is made to wait for the prep stream in that case.
+    """
+    target = out.device if out is not None else torch.device(device)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+    compute_stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(target)
+    prep = prep_stream(target)
+    with torch.cuda.stream(prep):
+        staged = src.to(device=target, non_blocking=True)
+    # Under Confidential Computing ``is_pinned()`` reports False even for
+    # pin_memory=True allocations, so it cannot be used to decide whether the
+    # upload is host-synchronous. Always order the compute stream after the
+    # prep stream; the event wait is negligible and correct in both cases.
+    compute_stream.wait_stream(prep)
+    staged.record_stream(compute_stream)
+    if out is None:
+        return staged
+    return out.copy_(staged, non_blocking=True)

+class StagedH2DBuffer:
+    """Explicit-copy fallback for NVIDIA Confidential Computing.
+

🚀

CC-hardware validation data for this PR's premise (this is not a review of the diff, and I have not yet tested this PR's head). The runs were AI-assisted (Claude Code); I ran them and reviewed the output.

**Setup:** Azure `Standard_NCC40ads_H100_v5` (H100 NVL), CC ON per `nvidia-smi conf-compute -f`, driver 595.71.05, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Qwen3-8B, random 1024/256 tokens.

1. **Host-synchronous copies confirmed on H100 NVL.** A standalone microbench (#60338, [results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60338#issuecomment-6041789699)) shows pinned H2D/D2H on a busy stream blocking the host for ~19.9 ms, vs ~51 us on an idle stream. A decode loop with staged H2D + D2H worker is x1.46 (3 ms forward) / x1.14 (10 ms) vs sync, while async scheduling alone is x1.00. Reproduced on two separate VMs.
2. **V1 with #52226's copy optimizations is correct and faster with async on.** Output tok/s at concurrency 4 / 32: async on 569 / 2864 vs 468-478 / 2519-2555 for async off or optimizations off (+12-19%).
3. **V2 under CC without a UVA guard returns wrong output.** On a branch with #52226 but not this PR, forced V2 and the V2 default both produced junk (URL fragments, runs of `!` and `1`) on 8/8 greedy prompts, while V1 was correct. That reproduces #57224 on H100 NVL, which this PR's UVA gating addresses.

**Offer:** I can run the same sweep plus the output check against `c8309e4215` on this hardware and post the results here.

**Question:** would you want PPCIe/NVLE-aware detection (`nvmlSystemGetConfComputeSettings`, `multiGpuMode`) as a small follow-up PR? My understanding is that Hopper PPCIe reports `ccFeature` OFF but still uses bounce buffers; I have not been able to test that mode.

Thank you @Alex-Carter01 for the detailed measurements!

The v1 patch PR is indeed not intended to resolve the garbage output under V2, **but this PR should** (along with performance improvements). 

It would be very helpful to get a third party validation of this PR, so a run against the current head on your H100 NVL would be much appreciated. Greedy coherence on all prompts plus tok/s at a couple of concurrencies is plenty.

@ybgao-nvidia Third-party validation of this PR on a different CC platform from @Alex-Carter01's. The setup is an Azure NCC H100 NVL with an **AMD SEV-SNP** guest and the GPU in CC mode, on the same machine type where #57224, #57562 and #57680 were reported.

**Setup.** `vllm==0.31.0` wheel, torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.0.post1 with the matching jit-cache, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (MoE), async scheduling on. The `vllm/` files of this PR's head (`5bb8a5cf`) were applied to the wheel; they applied cleanly. Three configs ran back to back on one VM, with a server restart between them.

| config | greedy output vs V1 | c=1 tok/s | c=12 tok/s | #57562 repro |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | reference | 145.8 (145.0–145.9) | 1275.3 (1253.5–1278.1) | 12/12, engine alive |
| V2, unpatched 0.31.0 | 0/8, unrelated tokens | 40.6 (40.6–61.7), bimodal | 318.7 (291.4–377.2) | EngineCore dies in round 1 (`num_output_placeholders >= 0`) |
| **V2 + this PR** | **8/8 byte-identical** | **243.0 (242.9–243.1)** | **1984.6 (1981.4–1986.2)** | 12/12, engine alive |

c=1 is per-stream decode tok/s and c=12 is aggregate output tok/s. Each request is 512 tokens with `ignore_eos`, median of 5 runs (range in brackets). The repro is the chunked-prefill concurrency script from #57562, run as 6 concurrent requests × 2 rounds.

The startup log shows the intended path: `NVIDIA Confidential Computing detected via NVML`, then `Using staged H2D input copies under Confidential Computing`, and `Using V2 Model Runner`.

With this PR, V2 under CC is correct and runs 67% faster than V1 at c=1 and 56% faster at c=12 on this model. Unpatched 0.31.0 still shows all three original symptoms.

I can re-run it on a later head if that would help.

Thank you @yeighta for the insights and measurements! I'm glad to see correctness and performance improvements also on H100. 

It would be also nice to measure on head-of-PR, but we should expect to see similar performance as what we previously observe.

@ybgao-nvidia as requested, here is a run on the current head (`5bb8a5cf43`) on H100 NVL, complementary to @yeighta's SEV-SNP / MoE result above. AI-assisted (Claude Code); I ran it and reviewed the results.

**Setup:** Azure `Standard_NCC40ads_H100_v5` (H100 NVL), CC ON, driver 595.71.05, torch 2.13.0+cu130, dense `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, random 1024/256 tokens, one run per arm. Precompiled wheel from the PR's base (`ce49174247`) with the PR's Python on top. `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` for every arm (the image has no nvcc).

| Arm | Config | Greedy match (8 prompts) | Output tok/s, c=4 | c=32 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stock | defaults (V2, async on) | reference, text is correct | 577 | 2327 |
| F1 | `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 --no-async-scheduling` | 8/8 | 444 | 2038 |
| control | `VLLM_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE=0` (CC path off while CC is on) | **0/8**, junk output | n/a | n/a |

So under CC, V2 with this PR returns correct text, and switching the CC path off on the same CC-on GPU reproduces the garbage output. Async on is +30% / +14% over async off at c=4 / 32.

An earlier run on the previous head (`c8309e4215`, a different VM) gave the same correctness result and 575 / 2759 (stock) and 442 / 2344 (async off), so c=4 is identical and c=32 is 13-16% lower on this VM for both arms. Both arms moved together, which looks like VM-to-VM variance rather than the one-commit change, but I can't separate the two from one run each.

**Limits:** one GPU model, one run per arm, so differences of a few percent are within noise; PPCIe/NVLE not tested. I'm happy to repeat the run or try another model if useful.
